transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess I’ve just been feeling… kind of constantly “on,” if that makes sense. Like I’ll finish one thing at school or at home, and instead of being able to sit down or shut off, I’m already jumping into the next thing. It’s probably not the worst problem, but lately it feels like I’m running on a motor most of the time, and I thought maybe I should ask about it.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual?

I don’t think so… not in any clear way. I mean, I might stay up later than I should sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m suddenly getting by on way less sleep and feeling fine. At least, I haven’t really noticed that. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you often have trouble paying attention, even when you’re trying to focus?

I’m not sure I’d say it’s attention exactly… I mean, I can usually focus when I really have to. Sometimes my mind wanders, sure, but I don’t know if it’s more than what other people deal with. Could you maybe say what kind of trouble paying attention you mean?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to worry?

I don’t think so, not a lot. I mean, I worry about normal things—work stuff, whether I handled something right—but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying for no reason. At least, I haven’t noticed it that way. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had times when your mood was unusually high or unusually irritable?

I don’t think I’ve had anything like an unusually high mood, no. Irritable… maybe I can get annoyed like anyone else, but I wouldn’t say it’s been unusual or out of character. At least not that I’ve noticed. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
Did you feel this same way as a child?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but my mother used to joke that even in elementary school I was “teaching the class from my seat.” I was apparently always popping up, talking, or jumping in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So, yes, I guess it was part of me pretty early on—not something that only started recently with the family changes. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you often act or speak before thinking, in ways that get you into trouble at school, work, or home?

Yeah… I suppose I do that more than I’d like to admit. I don’t usually mean it badly—I feel like I’m helping or clarifying—but I’ll jump into conversations with colleagues or parents before they’re done, or even at home with my spouse and a relative, and I end up talking over people or kind of taking charge too quickly.

It can cause tension, yes. I’m not proud of that. I often realize afterward that I should’ve waited and let them finish. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

latest_inference.note: Lifelong pattern since childhood of hyperactivity/impulsivity (always 'on,' popping up/talking in class, interrupting, acting before thinking) supports ADHD. Bipolar/manic causes are less likely given no decreased need for sleep, no elevated/irritable mood episodes, and chronic rather than episodic course. Stress-related diagnosis is not supported as primary because symptoms predate recent family changes.
